title: Daily Market Digest: August 28, 2026
subtitle: Friday's Session Sees Indices Dip After Fed Chair's Inflation Warning, Tech Earnings Mixed

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Retreat Slightly on Friday After Fed Chair Signals Potential Rate Hikes
items.summary: Major U.S. indices experienced a modest decline on Friday, as investors digested Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's comments from Jackson Hole, indicating that further interest rate hikes might be necessary to combat persistent inflation. This pullback followed a strong Thursday rally driven by robust NVIDIA earnings and broader AI optimism.

items.headline: NVIDIA Soars on Blowout Earnings and Bullish AI Forecast
items.summary: Shares of the semiconductor giant $NVDA surged 8.7% to $96.22 after the company reported strong Q2 2026 earnings of $2.22 per share, exceeding analyst estimates, and projected a robust 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, largely driven by demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure.

items.headline: Salesforce Jumps Following Earnings Beat
items.summary: Salesforce ($CRM) saw its stock climb 22.6% on the back of an earnings beat, contributing to broader tech sector strength.

items.headline: Elastic Surges After Strong Q1 Earnings
items.summary: Elastic N.V. ($ESTC) shares rallied 17% after the company reported higher-than-expected fiscal Q1 non-GAAP earnings and revenue, indicating strong performance in its cloud software offerings.

items.headline: Gap Rises on Upbeat Guidance and New Old Navy CEO
items.summary: The Gap, Inc. ($GAP) shares jumped 13% after the retailer raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings guidance and announced a new CEO for its Old Navy brand, signaling positive strategic moves despite mixed Q2 2026 results.

items.headline: PayPal Plunges as Takeover Bid Collapses
items.summary: PayPal ($PYPL) shares fell 13% after Bloomberg reported that private equity firm Advent and payments company Stripe abandoned their $50 billion takeover bid for the fintech company, removing a key catalyst for the stock.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Falls on Revenue Timing Concerns
items.summary: Marvell Technology ($MRVL) saw its shares drop over 10% despite reporting stronger-than-expected fiscal Q2 results, as investor concerns mounted regarding the timing of revenue from its significant deal with Alphabet's Google.

items.headline: Build-A-Bear Workshop Leads Thursday's Losers
items.summary: Build-A-Bear Workshop ($BBW) experienced a significant decline of 27.3%, making it one of the weakest performers among market movers.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh Signals Further Rate Hikes at Jackson Hole Amid Stubborn Inflation
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh, in his debut speech at the annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, delivered a hawkish message, stating that inflation remains 'stubbornly above the central bank's 2% target' and implying that the Fed 'may have to raise interest rates in the coming months' to bring it under control. The bond market reacted with building expectations for rate hikes, pushing the two-year Treasury yield higher.

items.headline: Technology Sector Experiences Mixed Fortunes; AI Chip Export Controls Eyed
items.summary: After a robust Thursday rally driven by NVIDIA's strong performance, the tech sector saw a downturn on Friday, with the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF ($XLK) falling 1.5% and the State Street SPDR S&P Semiconductor ETF ($XSD) dropping 3.9%. This comes as the Department of Commerce works on a new plan to control advanced AI chip exports, aiming to close loopholes allowing Chinese firms access.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Drops in August on Persistent Inflation Worries
items.summary: U.S. consumer sentiment declined in August, with the main index falling 6.3% to 51.7 from July. The drop reflects ongoing concerns among consumers that inflation will remain elevated for the 'foreseeable future'.

items.headline: Jobless Claims Continue to Decline, Signaling Tight Labor Market
items.summary: Initial jobless claims for the week ending August 22 totaled 203,000, a decrease of 4,000 from the previous week. This sustained low level of claims, along with steady continuing claims, suggests a persistent tightness in the labor market.
